Main.sentence: Edward Moore Kennedy (February 22, 1932 – August 25, 2009) was an American lawyer and politician from ___E:Massachusetts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massachusetts)___ who served as a member of the ___E:United States Senate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate)___ from 1962 to his death in 2009. A member of the ___E:Democratic Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States))___ and the prominent ___E:Kennedy family U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_family)___ , he was the ___E:second-most-senior U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_United_States_Senators_in_the_111th_Congress_by_seniority)___ member of the Senate when he died. He is ___E:ranked fifth in U.S. history for length of continuous service as a senator U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_members_of_the_United_States_Congress_by_longevity_of_service#U.S._Senate_time)___ .

Kennedy was the younger brother of President ___E:John F. Kennedy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy)___ and U.S. attorney general and U.S. senator ___E:Robert F. Kennedy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy)___ , and the father of U.S. representative ___E:Patrick J. Kennedy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrick_J._Kennedy)___ .

After attending ___E:Harvard University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvard_University)___ and earning his law degree from the ___E:University of Virginia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Virginia)___ , Kennedy began his career as an assistant district attorney in ___E:Suffolk County, Massachusetts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suffolk_County,_Massachusetts)___ .

He won a ___E:November 1962 special election in Massachusetts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1962_United_States_Senate_special_election_in_Massachusetts)___ to fill the vacant seat previously held by his brother John, who had taken office as the U.S. president.
He was ___E:elected to a full six-year term in 1964 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1964_United_States_Senate_election_in_Massachusetts)___ and was re-elected seven more times.

After the ___E:Chappaquiddick incident U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chappaquiddick_incident)___ in 1969 resulted in the death of his automobile passenger, ___E:Mary Jo Kopechne U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary_Jo_Kopechne)___ , Kennedy pleaded guilty to a charge of leaving the scene of an accident and received a two-month ___E:suspended sentence U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suspended_sentence)___ .
The incident and its aftermath hindered his chances of becoming president.

He ran in 1980 in the ___E:Democratic primary campaign U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1980_Democratic_Party_presidential_primaries)___ for the party's nomination, but lost to the incumbent president, ___E:Jimmy Carter U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Carter)___ .
Kennedy was known for his ___E:oratorical skills U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_speaking)___ .

His 1968 eulogy for his brother Robert and his ___E:1980 rallying cry U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dream_Shall_Never_Die)___ for ___E:modern American liberalism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_American_liberalism)___ were among his best-known speeches.
He became recognized as "The Lion of the Senate" through his long tenure and influence.

Kennedy and his staff wrote more than 300 bills that were enacted into law. Unabashedly liberal, Kennedy championed an interventionist government that emphasized ___E:economic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic_justice)___ and ___E:social justice U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_justice)___ , but he was also known for working with Republicans to find compromises.

Kennedy played a major role in passing many laws, including the ___E:Immigration and Nationality Act of 1965 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immigration_and_Nationality_Act_of_1965)___ , the ___E:National Cancer Act of 1971 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Cancer_Act_of_1971)___ , the ___E:COBRA health insurance provision U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consolidated_Omnibus_Budget_Reconciliation_Act_of_1985)___ , the ___E:Comprehensive Anti-Apartheid Act of 1986 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comprehensive_Anti-Apartheid_Act_of_1986)___ , the ___E:Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Americans_with_Disabilities_Act_of_1990)___ , the ___E:Ryan White AIDS Care Act U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_White_AIDS_Care_Act)___ , the ___E:Civil Rights Act of 1991 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_Rights_Act_of_1991)___ , the ___E:Mental Health Parity Act U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mental_Health_Parity_Act)___ , the ___E:S-CHIP children's health program U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_Children%27s_Health_Insurance_Program)___ , the ___E:No Child Left Behind Act U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No_Child_Left_Behind_Act)___ , and the ___E:Edward M. Kennedy Serve America Act U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_M._Kennedy_Serve_America_Act)___ .
During the 2000s, he led several unsuccessful ___E:immigration reform U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immigration_reform)___ efforts.
Over the course of his Senate career, Kennedy made efforts to enact ___E:universal health care U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_health_care)___ , which he called the "cause of my life".
By his later years, Kennedy had come to be viewed as a major figure and spokesman for ___E:American progressivism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_progressivism)___ .

On August 25, 2009, Kennedy died of a ___E:brain tumor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain_tumor)___ ( ___E:glioblastoma U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glioblastoma)___ ) at his home in ___E:Hyannis Port, Massachusetts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyannis_Port,_Massachusetts)___ , at the age of 77. He was buried at ___E:Arlington National Cemetery U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arlington_National_Cemetery)___ .

Edward Moore Kennedy was born at St. Margaret's Hospital in the ___E:Dorchester U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorchester,_Boston)___ section of ___E:Boston, Massachusetts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston,_Massachusetts)___ on February 22, 1932. He was the youngest of the nine children of ___E:Joseph Patrick Kennedy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_Patrick_Kennedy)___ and ___E:Rose Fitzgerald U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rose_Fitzgerald)___ , members of prominent ___E:Irish-American U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Irish_Americans_in_Boston)___ families in Boston.
They constituted one of the wealthiest families in the nation after their marriage.

His eight siblings were ___E:Joseph Jr. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_P._Kennedy_Jr.)___ , ___E:John U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy)___ , ___E:Rose U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosemary_Kennedy)___ , ___E:Kathleen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kathleen_Cavendish,_Marchioness_of_Hartington)___ , ___E:Eunice U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eunice_Kennedy_Shriver)___ , ___E:Patricia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patricia_Kennedy_Lawford)___ , ___E:Robert U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy)___ , and ___E:Jean U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean_Kennedy_Smith)___ .

His older brother John asked to be the newborn's godfather, a request his parents honored, though they did not agree to his request to name the baby George Washington Kennedy (Kennedy was born on President ___E:George Washington U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Washington)___ 's 200th birthday).
They named the boy after their father's assistant and longtime friend.

As a child, Kennedy was frequently uprooted by his family's moves among ___E:Bronxville, New York U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bronxville,_New_York)___ ; ___E:Hyannis Port, Massachusetts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyannis_Port,_Massachusetts)___ ; ___E:Palm Beach, Florida U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palm_Beach,_Florida)___ ; and the ___E:Court of St. James's U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Court_of_St._James%27s)___ , in ___E:London U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London)___ , England.
His formal education started at Gibbs School in Kensington, London.
He had attended 10 schools by the age of eleven; these disruptions interfered with his academic success.

He was an ___E:altar boy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Altar_boy)___ at the ___E:St. Joseph's Church U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Church_of_St._Joseph_(Bronxville,_New_York))___ and was seven when he received his ___E:First Communion U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Communion)___ from ___E:Pope Pius XII U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Pius_XII)___ in the ___E:Vatican U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apostolic_Palace)___ .

He spent sixth and seventh grades at the ___E:Fessenden School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fessenden_School)___ , where he was a mediocre student,  and eighth grade at Cranwell Preparatory School, both in ___E:Massachusetts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massachusetts)___ .
He was the youngest child and his parents were affectionate toward him, but they also compared him unfavorably with his older brothers.

Between the ages of eight and sixteen, Kennedy suffered the traumas of his sister Rosemary's failed ___E:lobotomy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lobotomy)___ and the deaths of two siblings: Joseph Jr. in an airplane explosion and Kathleen in an airplane crash.

Kennedy's affable maternal grandfather, ___E:John F. Fitzgerald U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Fitzgerald)___ , was the ___E:Mayor of Boston U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayor_of_Boston)___ , a U.S.
Congressman, and an early political and personal influence.

Kennedy spent his four high-school years at ___E:Milton Academy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milton_Academy)___ , a preparatory school in ___E:Milton, Massachusetts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milton,_Massachusetts)___ , where he received B and C grades.

In 1950, he finished 36th in a graduating class of 56.  He did well at ___E:football U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_football)___ there, playing on the varsity in his last two years; the school's headmaster later described his play as "absolutely fearless ... he would have tackled an express train to New York if you asked ... he loved contact sports".
Kennedy also played on the tennis team and was in the drama, debate, and glee clubs.
Like his father and brothers before him, Ted graduated from ___E:Harvard College U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvard_College)___ .
In his spring semester, he was assigned to the athlete-oriented ___E:Winthrop House U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winthrop_House)___ , where his brothers had also lived.
He was an ___E:offensive and defensive end U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/End_(American_football))___ on the freshman football team; his play was characterized by his large size and fearless style.
In his first semester, Kennedy and his classmates arranged to copy answers from another student during the final examination for a science class.

At the end of his second semester in May 1951, Kennedy was anxious about maintaining his eligibility for athletics for the next year,  and he had a classmate take his place at a ___E:Spanish U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_language)___ exam.   The ruse was discovered and both were expelled for cheating.
As was standard for serious disciplinary cases, they were told they could apply for readmission within a year or two if they demonstrated good behavior during that time.

In June 1951, Kennedy enlisted in the ___E:United States Army U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Army)___ and signed up for an optional four-year term that was shortened to the minimum of two years after his father intervened.

Following ___E:basic training U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Army_Basic_Training)___ at ___E:Fort Dix U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Dix)___ in ___E:New Jersey U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Jersey)___ , he requested assignment to ___E:Fort Holabird U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Holabird)___ in ___E:Maryland U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maryland)___ for ___E:Army Intelligence U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_Intelligence_Corps_(United_States_Army))___ training, but was dropped without explanation after a few weeks.

He went to ___E:Camp Gordon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camp_Gordon)___ in ___E:Georgia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_(U.S._state))___ for training in the ___E:Military Police Corps U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_Police_Corps_(United_States_Army))___ .

In June 1952, Kennedy was assigned to the ___E:honor guard U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guard_of_honour)___ at ___E:SHAPE U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Headquarters_Allied_Powers_Europe)___ headquarters in Paris, France.
His father's political connections ensured that he was not deployed to the ongoing ___E:Korean War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_War)___ .

While stationed in Europe, Kennedy traveled extensively on weekends and climbed the ___E:Matterhorn U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matterhorn)___ in the ___E:Pennine Alps U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pennine_Alps)___ .
After 21 months, he was discharged in March 1953 as a ___E:private first class U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Private_first_class#United_States_Army)___ .
Kennedy re-entered Harvard in the summer of 1953 and improved his study habits.
His brother John was a U.S.
Senator and the family was attracting more public attention.

Kennedy joined ___E:The Owl U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Owl_Club_(Harvard))___ ___E:final club U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Final_club)___ in 1954  and was also chosen for the ___E:Hasty Pudding Club U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hasty_Pudding_Club)___ and the Pi Eta fraternity.

Kennedy was on athletic probation during his sophomore year, and he returned as a second-string two-way end for the ___E:Crimson football team U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvard_Crimson_football)___ during his junior year. He barely missed earning his ___E:varsity letter U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varsity_letter)___ .  ___E:Green Bay Packers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Bay_Packers)___ head coach ___E:Lisle Blackbourn U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lisle_Blackbourn)___ asked him about his interest in playing professional football.

Kennedy demurred, saying he had plans to attend law school and "go into another contact sport, politics."  In his senior season of 1955, Kennedy started at end for the Harvard football team and worked hard to improve his blocking and tackling to complement his 6 ft 2 in (1.88 m), 200 lb (91 kg) size.  In the season-ending ___E:Harvard–Yale game U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvard-Yale_football_games_(The_Game))___ in the snow at the ___E:Yale Bowl U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yale_Bowl)___ on November 19 (which Yale won 21–7), Kennedy caught a pass to score Harvard's only touchdown;  the team finished the season with a 3–4–1 record.
Academically, Kennedy received mediocre grades for his first three years, improved to a B average for his senior year, and finished barely in the top half of his class.
Kennedy graduated from Harvard at age 24 in 1956 with an ___E:AB U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Arts)___ in history and government.
Due to his low grades, Kennedy was not accepted by ___E:Harvard Law School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvard_Law_School)___ .

He instead followed his brother Robert and enrolled in the ___E:University of Virginia School of Law U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Virginia_School_of_Law)___ in 1956.  That acceptance was controversial among faculty and alumni, who judged Kennedy's past cheating episodes to be incompatible with the University of Virginia's honor code; it took a full faculty vote to admit him.  Kennedy also attended ___E:The Hague Academy of International Law U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hague_Academy_of_International_Law)___ during one summer.

At Virginia, Kennedy felt that he had to study "four times as hard and four times as long" as other students to keep up.  He received mostly C grades  and was in the middle of the class ranking, but won the prestigious William Minor Lile Moot Court Competition.
He was elected head of the Student Legal Forum and brought many prominent speakers to the campus via his family connections.

While there, his questionable automotive practices were curtailed when he was charged with ___E:reckless driving U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reckless_driving)___ and ___E:driving without a license U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Driving_without_a_license)___ .

He was officially named as manager of his brother John's ___E:1958 Senate re-election campaign U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1958_United_States_Senate_elections)___ ; Ted's ability to connect with ordinary voters on the street helped bring a record-setting victory margin that gave credibility to John's presidential aspirations.
Kennedy graduated from law school in 1959.

In October 1957 (early in his second year of law school), Kennedy met ___E:Joan Bennett U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joan_Bennett_Kennedy)___ at ___E:Manhattanville College U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manhattanville_College)___ ; they were introduced after a dedication speech for a gymnasium that his family had donated at the campus.
Bennett was a senior at Manhattanville and had worked as a model and won beauty contests, but she was unfamiliar with politics.
After the couple became engaged, she grew nervous about marrying someone she did not know that well, but Joe Kennedy insisted that the wedding should proceed.

The couple was married by ___E:Cardinal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_(Catholicism))___ ___E:Francis Spellman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francis_Spellman)___ on November 29, 1958, at ___E:St. Joseph's Church U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Church_of_St._Joseph_(Bronxville))___ in ___E:Bronxville, New York U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bronxville,_New_York)___ ,   with the reception being held at the nearby ___E:Siwanoy Country Club U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siwanoy_Country_Club)___ .

Ted and Joan had three children: ___E:Kara U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kara_Kennedy)___ (1960–2011), ___E:Edward Jr. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_M._Kennedy_Jr.)___ (b. 1961) and ___E:Patrick U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrick_J._Kennedy)___ (b. 1967).

By the 1970s, the marriage was in trouble due to Ted's ___E:infidelity U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infidelity)___ and Joan's growing ___E:alcoholism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alcoholism)___ .

Ted and Joan established ___E:Massachusetts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massachusetts)___ residency after buying a townhouse on Charles River Square in ___E:Boston U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston)___ , and a home on Squaw Island, ___E:Cape Cod U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_Cod)___ .
During Ted's tenure in the U.S.

Senate, the Kennedys lived in a townhouse in ___E:Georgetown U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgetown_(Washington,_D.C.))___ , Washington, D.C., and later, a 12,500-square-foot house in ___E:McLean, Virginia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLean,_Virginia)___ .

From 1982 until his death in 2009, the ___E:Kennedy Compound U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Compound)___ in ___E:Hyannis Port, Massachusetts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyannis_Port,_Massachusetts)___ became Ted's principal residence.
In 1959, Kennedy was admitted to the ___E:Massachusetts Bar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massachusetts_Bar_Association)___ .

In 1960, Ted's brother John announced his candidacy for ___E:President of the United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1960_United_States_presidential_election)___ and Ted managed his campaign in the Western states.

Kennedy learned to fly and during the ___E:Democratic primary campaign U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States)_presidential_primaries,_1960)___ he barnstormed around the western states, meeting with delegates and bonding with them by trying his hand at ___E:ski jumping U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ski_jumping)___ and ___E:bronc riding U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bronc_riding)___ .

The seven weeks he spent in ___E:Wisconsin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wisconsin)___ helped his brother win the first contested primary of the season there and a similar time spent in ___E:Wyoming U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming)___ was rewarded when a unanimous vote from that state's delegates put his brother over the top at the ___E:1960 Democratic National Convention U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1960_Democratic_National_Convention)___ .
Following his victory in the presidential election, John resigned from his seat as U.S.

Senator from Massachusetts, but Ted was not eligible to fill the vacancy until his thirtieth birthday on February 22, 1962.  Kennedy initially wanted to stay out west rather than run for office right away; he said, "The disadvantage of my position is being constantly compared with two brothers of such superior ability."  Kennedy's brothers were not in favor of his running immediately, but Kennedy ultimately coveted the Senate seat as an accomplishment to match his brothers, and their father overruled them.  John asked Massachusetts governor ___E:Foster Furcolo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foster_Furcolo)___ to name Kennedy family friend ___E:Ben Smith U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benjamin_A._Smith_II)___ as interim senator for John's unexpired term, which he did in December 1960.  This kept the seat available for Ted.

Meanwhile, Kennedy started work in February 1961 as an ___E:assistant district attorney U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assistant_district_attorney)___ at the ___E:Suffolk County, Massachusetts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suffolk_County,_Massachusetts)___ District Attorney's Office (for which he took a nominal ___E:$1 salary U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One-dollar_salary)___ ), where he developed a hard-nosed attitude towards crime.
He took many overseas trips, billed as fact-finding tours with the goal of improving his foreign policy credentials.

On a nine-nation ___E:Latin American U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_American)___ trip in 1961, FBI reports from the time showed Kennedy meeting with ___E:Lauchlin Currie U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lauchlin_Currie)___ , an alleged former Soviet spy, together with locals in each country whom the reports deemed left-wingers and Communist sympathizers.

Reports from the FBI and other sources had Kennedy renting a brothel and opening up bordellos after hours during the tour.    The Latin American trip helped to formulate Kennedy's foreign policy views, and in subsequent Boston Globe columns he warned that the region might turn to communism if the U.S. did not reach out to it in a more effective way.   Kennedy also began speaking to local political organizations.

In the ___E:1962 U.S. Senate special election in Massachusetts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1962_United_States_Senate_special_election_in_Massachusetts)___ , Kennedy initially faced a Democratic Party primary challenge from ___E:Edward J. McCormack Jr. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_J._McCormack_Jr.)___ , the ___E:state Attorney General U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massachusetts_Attorney_General)___ .
Kennedy's slogan was "He can do more for Massachusetts", the same one his brother John had used in his first campaign for the seat ten years earlier.

McCormack had the support of many liberals and intellectuals, who thought Kennedy inexperienced and knew of his suspension from Harvard, a fact which became public during the race.  Kennedy also faced the notion that with one brother President and another ___E:U.S. Attorney General U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Attorney_General)___ , "Don't you think that Teddy is one Kennedy too many?" But Kennedy proved to be an effective street-level campaigner.
His charm was such that one delegate at the party convention said "He's completely unqualified and inexperienced.
And I'm going to be with him".

In a televised debate, McCormack said "The office of United States Senator should be merited, and not inherited", and said that if his opponent's name was Edward Moore, not Edward Moore Kennedy, his candidacy "would be a joke".

Voters thought McCormack was overbearing—a Kennedy supporter said "McCormack was able to make a millionaire an underdog"  —and with the family political machine's finally getting fully behind him, Kennedy won the September 1962 primary by a two-to-one margin.
